chunks: Fear Him who has bestowed on you what you know,

key_terms.أَمَدَّكُمْ: He bestowed upon you / He prolonged your supply
key_terms.بَمَا: With what / by means of which

ai.seo_question: What does it mean that God 'amaddakum' (bestowed/prolonged) upon you in Surah Ash-Shu'ara?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the concept of 'Ibadah' (worship) through gratitude for the 'Ma'lum' (known) blessings, particularly intellect and provision, which distinguish humans from other creatures. The phrase 'Amaddakum' implies a continuous divine support, urging believers to maintain consciousness of God amidst the abundance of familiar favors. This serves as a reminder that neglecting these known blessings is a form of ingratitude that leads to spiritual decline.
